messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: performance & SLO checklist (ACMEPAY)

Thanks again for taking the time to demo with us today — really appreciate the candid discussion on production constraints. Per our ask, attaching a short SLO checklist and a summary of the performance targets we captured during the call. Please review and confirm the points below so we can build the mutual action plan (MAP).

Attachment: [slo-checklist.pdf] (See summary table on page 2)
Attachment: [perf-samples.jsonl] (sample request traces)

Key SLO items (please confirm):
- Latency target (P95): 150ms for standard conversational requests (avg request length ~120 tokens).
- Tail latency (P99): <= 300ms for interactive flows.
- Throughput: steady-state 120 QPS for async non-streaming endpoints across peak hour.
- Concurrency: support 250 concurrent active sessions (concurrency defined as distinct in-flight requests).
- Streaming: required for the customer-facing chat UI for slow multimodal responses — client expects server-sent events at token granularity.
- Burst capacity: up to 300 QPS for 10 minutes during batch billing cycles.

Open questions / clarifications we need from your side:
1) Confirm whether the 150ms P95 is for streaming responses (first-byte) or for full completion.
2) Typical prompt and response sizes for summary vs. full-resolution flows (samples appreciated).
3) Any regulatory constraints for data leaving your VPC (for private deployment discussion).

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood to verify config for streaming-first-byte vs completion latency and share a short perf note (Michael and Aditya on copy).
- Customer to send a representative sample of peak-hour traces (we received a few in perf-samples.jsonl but need more).
- Agree on decision criteria by 2026-08-25 so we can scope Dedicated capacity recommendation.

If the SLOs above match what you discussed internally, reply with the confirmation and any missing sample traces. Happy to hop on a 30-minute follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. A few quick confirmations from our side:
- 150ms P95 target is for first-byte latency on streaming responses (we care most about time-to-first-token in the chat UI).
- P99 goal 300ms is for first-byte as well.
- Throughput: 120 QPS steady-state is correct for our high-volume midnight batch-related windows, but our daytime peak may spike to 140 QPS occasionally.
- Concurrency: 250 is fine; we already run a session-per-user model and that tracks.
- Streaming: required, yes — token-level SSE is what our frontend expects.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm batching behavior for streaming endpoints? We don’t want batching to delay first-byte.
2) For Dedicated, what’s the recommended headroom you size for bursts (we saw \"burst capacity\" in your notes)?

We’ll pull additional traces and send later today. If you can send the perf note on streaming behavior, that will help us validate with infra.

— Taylor

Hi Taylor — quick notes from infra/serving runtime side (answers inline):

1) Batching & streaming first-byte behavior:
- For streaming endpoints we disable application-level minibatching for first-byte. Our runtime prioritizes first-token generation paths and will stream the first token within the normal single-request latency bound. Subsequent token generation uses continuous KV cache and opportunistic batching but that does not delay first-byte.
- Recommendation: set streaming=true and set max_batch_size=8 for steady-state to balance throughput/latency.

2) Burst sizing / headroom:
- If you expect 140 QPS occasional spikes, we recommend Dedicated sizing for 160 QPS steady-state with autoscale headroom to 320 QPS for short bursts (10–15 minutes). That maps to 6x A100-equivalent GPUs in our benchmarked config for your workload profile (median sequence length ~120 tokens).

3) Concurrency semantics:
- Our platform counts concurrency as in-flight requests. For session-per-user patterns we suggest connection pooling at the client to keep concurrent in-flight requests below 300 to avoid increased queuing.

4) Sample perf numbers (from our internal run vs your perf-samples.jsonl):
- Streaming first-token P50: 28ms, P95: 120ms, P99: 210ms (on 160 QPS config).
- Completion latency P95 (full response): 420ms for 120 token responses.

Attachments: [perf-samples.jsonl] (annotated with request ids)

Let us know if you want a short(30m) runbook call where we walk through the Dedicated sizing and autoscale policy. If you confirm the decision criteria we can draft a MAP with milestones for infra setup, validation, and procurement.

Thanks,

Thanks for the quick confirmations, Taylor — and great detail, Michael. Per the thread, here’s the proposed MAP and decision criteria so we can keep this moving: 

MAP (proposed milestones):
- 2026-08-25: AcmePay confirms decision criteria (latency semantics, throughput headroom, streaming required).
- 2026-08-27: Redwood provides Dedicated sizing proposal + preliminary pricing (based on 160 QPS steady-state, autoscale to 320 QPS).
- 2026-09-02: Joint validation run (48-hour soak) with representative traces and perf instrumentation.
- 2026-09-10: Finalize contract / reserved capacity commitment.

Decision criteria checklist (please reply YES to each to confirm):
- We agree streaming SLOs refer to first-byte latency (P95 <= 150ms).
- We accept the recommended Dedicated sizing with autoscale headroom to 320 QPS for bursts.
- We will supply additional peak-hour traces by 2026-08-23.
- No data residency blocking issues for Redwood-managed Dedicated in AWS us-east-1 (we have a Private option if needed).

If you can confirm the four items above, we’ll lock the proposal timeline and I’ll set up the pricing doc and runbook call (Michael to lead the validation run). Happy to adjust timeline if you need more time — just let me know.

Thanks,
